about.summary: Own the stock while its price is above its 200-day (about 10-month) average; step aside when it closes below. Best run on monthly candles (Candle 1M), as Faber did.
about.why: Mebane Faber's widely cited 2007 paper showed that holding an asset only while it is above its 10-month average gave returns similar to buy & hold with much smaller drawdowns, across US stocks and other asset classes back to 1900. Jeremy Siegel tested a 200-day average rule on the Dow with similar conclusions about risk, and Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) document "time-series momentum": assets that have been rising tend to keep rising for a while.
about.caveats: Designed for broad indexes and asset classes; single stocks are noisier, so expect more false exits. On daily candles it trades far more often than intended. In a fast crash it reacts only after the fall has started, and it usually lags buy & hold in long bull markets.
references: Faber, M. T. (2007). A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation. The Journal of Wealth Management, 9(4), 69-79.
Siegel, J. J. (2014). Stocks for the Long Run (5th ed.). McGraw-Hill.
Moskowitz, T. J., Ooi, Y. H., & Pedersen, L. H. (2012). Time Series Momentum. Journal of Financial Economics, 104(2), 228-250.
